prompt: A furniture maker's on-time delivery rate fell from 95% to 80%. The candidate's framework: (1) Order planning and scheduling; (2) Production delays in the factory; (3) Shipping and carrier delays. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Missing: late materials from suppliers before production
options.feedback: Right. Late raw materials are a common cause of late deliveries, and they sit before every stage in this framework.

options.text: Buckets 2 and 3 overlap: both are physical delays in moving furniture
options.feedback: A delay in the factory and a delay with the carrier happen at different stages and have different fixes.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: carriers are outside the client's control
options.feedback: Carrier delays still make deliveries late, and the client can choose or manage its carriers.

options.text: It's a generic process map: it never asks which furniture lines are late
options.feedback: Splitting by product line can be done inside each stage. A process view is the right start. The flaw is a missing stage.

explanation: Follow the order from start to finish: order intake, materials, production, shipping. The upstream stages are missing.

extras.corrected_framework: Order intake and planning; supplier materials; production; shipping and delivery
